description:
Responsibilities
Peraton is seeking a Senior Full Stack Engineer to support the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Volcano Hazards Program (VHP). In this role, you will serve as an embedded technical contributor within the VHP government team, designing, developing, documenting, and deploying a modern, cloud-ready database and associated data visualization tools that support the program’s monitoring and evaluation (M&E) workflows. Your work will directly enable scientists, program managers, and stakeholders across the five U.S. volcano observatories and the Volcano Disaster Assistance Program (VDAP) to track performance, visualize geospatial hazard data, and produce evidence-based reports.
Work Location : Remote
Day to Day Roles and Responsibilities:

• Database Design & Development - Analyze government-furnished M&E plans and existing VDAP M&E database code; design and implement a relational database (PostgreSQL/PostGIS) supporting VHP monitoring and evaluation data; develop stored procedures, views, data validation logic, and comprehensive data dictionaries; architect the database for mobile device accessibility.

• API & Backend Development - Design and implement RESTful APIs in Python (FastAPI or Flask) to expose database functionality; develop data ingestion tools and ETL workflows to load M&E data from existing sources; implement metadata management aligned with USGS standards; conduct unit and integration testing of all backend components.

• Front-End & Visualization Development - Develop a web-based and mobile-friendly data entry and reporting interface using JavaScript/TypeScript and React; create an easily editable content management tool allowing VHP staff to update the M&E framework without developer intervention; build interactive dashboards and visualization modules for M&E analysis and reporting with filtering, drill-down, and export capabilities.

• GIS & Geospatial Visualization - Develop GIS-enabled tools for spatial visualization of volcano data tied to M&E evaluation criteria; implement interactive web mapping using ESRI JavaScript API, Leaflet, or Mapbox; integrate geospatial layers with the database backend via RESTful APIs; leverage ArcGIS, ArcPy, GDAL/OGR, and PostGIS spatial functions.

• Cloud Readiness & Architecture - Architect all systems to be cloud-ready, portable, and maintainable, aligned with USGS approved architecture and security baselines; document deployment configurations for future migration to CHS-supported cloud and hybrid environments.

• Documentation - Produce and maintain all required documentation including user guides, data dictionaries, API references, system schemas, and deployment guides; follow USGS coding and documentation standards throughout.

• Security & Compliance - Complete required DOI security awareness training; adhere to FISMA, NIST, and DOI security requirements; support Certification and Accreditation (C&A) activities; confirm all web-based applications include USGS-approved logon banners; report any computer security incidents per DOI procedures.

• Section 508 Accessibility - Validate all web-based interfaces against WCAG 2.0 Level A and Level AA success criteria; apply universal design principles including semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, color contrast, and screen reader compatibility; remediate any non-conforming features.

• Collaboration & Communication - Attend and actively participate in weekly check-in meetings with VHP staff and the volcano-hazards software development team; provide written progress updates (work completed, planned, issues, risks); integrate feedback from the VHP Coordinator and COR; coordinate with teams across the five U.S. volcano observatories to maintain system interoperability.

title: Chemical Engineer @Diluvian (backed by Hexa)
description:
About Diluvian

Diluvian builds containerized atmospheric water generators (10ft units) that produce drinking water from ambient air,

off-grid, for defense, mining and remote industrial sites. The company is incubated by Hexa, the Brussels-based

venture studio, and the first units go into the field in the coming months.

Why MOFs

Our first units run on a proven silica-gel desiccant, so we can ship fast and learn from real deployments. The next

step is metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). Water-stable MOFs such as aluminium fumarate (e.g. Basolite A520)

show a steep uptake step at low-to-mid relative humidity and regenerate at lower temperature than classical

desiccants. That could mean more litres per kWh and per kg of sorbent, especially in arid conditions. Your role is to

turn that potential into validated, system-level data that drives our next unit generation.

What you'll do

• Co-design and build a water sorption test setup (humidity-controlled chamber, cycling bench, instrumentation) with

our engineering team

• Source and benchmark commercial MOFs (e.g. BASF, Promethean Particles, NovoMOF) against our silica-gel

baseline

• Measure water sorption isotherms, adsorption/desorption kinetics and regeneration temperature under realistic

conditions (temperature, RH, cycle times)

• Run accelerated cycling tests (hundreds to thousands of cycles) to quantify capacity loss and structural stability

• Explore shaping and integration: pellets, binders, coatings on heat-exchanger or wheel supports, and the

performance hit each implies

• Check water quality: metal and linker leaching against EU drinking water limits (Directive 2020/2184)

• Translate results into system-level numbers (L/kWh, L/kg sorbent/day, €/kg at scale) and clear material

recommendations for our engineering team

How we work

• Freelance, part-time, over the coming weeks and months; evenings and weekends are fine

• You won't build alone: our engineering team supports you hands-on on test-rig design, hardware and

instrumentation

• Characterization runs in partner labs we have access to; you help decide which tests are worth running where

• You set your own experimental plan and milestones, and own the results. We provide context, budget and fast

decisions

• You'll work directly with Diluvian's founders, Quentin Van Overmeere (CTO) and Arnaud Biebuyck (CEO)

Who we're looking for

• MSc in chemistry, chemical engineering or materials science; PhD students and recent graduates welcome

• Hands-on lab experience, ideally with porous materials, adsorption or materials characterization (DVS, BET, XRD,

TGA)

• High agency: you design the experiments, drive them to results, and tell us what the data means

• Bonus: familiarity with sorption-based AWG literature (MOF-801, MOF-303, Al-fumarate) or thermal systems

About the Internet Society Foundation
The Internet Society (ISOC) supports and promotes the development of the Internet as a global technical infrastructure, a resource to enrich people’s lives, and a force for good in society. Our work aligns with our goals for the Internet to be open, globally connected, secure, and trustworthy. We seek collaboration with all who share these goals.
Together, we focus on building and supporting the communities that make the Internet work; advancing the development and application of Internet infrastructure, technologies, and open standards; and advocating for policy that is consistent with our view of the Internet.
The Internet Society Foundation (Foundation) is a non-profit organization that works in concert with the Internet Society . It exists to demonstrate and support the positive difference the Internet can make to people everywhere and promote the development of the Internet as a global technical infrastructure, a resource to enrich people’s lives, and a force for good in society.
The Foundation is committed to a culture of diversity and inclusion, where all individuals are valued for their distinct contributions. Our people are the most valuable strengths we have. The collective sum of the individual differences, life experiences, knowledge, inventiveness, innovation, self-expression, unique capabilities and talent that our staff invests in their work represents a significant part of not only our culture, but our reputation and the Foundation's achievements.
About the Position
The Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Specialist plays a critical role in supporting the Foundation team as we advance our systems. This position works closely and collaboratively with members of the Philanthropy and Empowerment teams and directly supports the Director, Learning, Evaluation & Impact in ensuring that programs and funded projects are collecting data, supporting analysis efforts to identify results achieved, communicating results, and facilitating learning from data collected. The MEL Specialist will also contribute to the Foundation's capacity building efforts for staff and grantees, particularly in designing and conducting trainings on monitoring, evaluation and learning for staff and partners. The MEL Specialist combines a working knowledge of technical MEL practices with excellent communication and collaboration skills.
The Foundation is a small team of passionate, collaborative, and driven staff that depend on each other to move our mission forward; this is true of this critical position.
The MEL Specialist will collaborate across the program portfolio, manage multiple priorities, and support internal and external stakeholders. This role requires strong communication, adaptability, and the ability to thrive in a dynamic, globally diverse environment. A track record of teamwork, initiative, and resourcefulness is essential.

Remote at home location

• Provide technical support for the Foundation’s monitoring, evaluation and learning efforts, primarily to program staff.

• Contribute to assessments and evaluations of Foundation projects, including designing evaluation methodologies, sampling strategies and data collection tools, collecting and analyzing data, and communicating findings in user-friendly formats.

• Support the design and implementation of learning and adaptation initiatives for program teams, including facilitating reflection sessions.

• Provide guidance and assistance [including report writing and infographics development] in data collection and data analysis (both quantitative and qualitative) on assessments and evaluations conducted by M&E and program team.
